name: Player
desc: Updates the player's position on the server. Has subclasses for different update types.

subclasses.name: C04PacketPlayerPosition
subclasses.desc: Position update (x, y, z) with onGround.

subclasses.name: C06PacketPlayerPosLook
subclasses.desc: Full position + rotation update with onGround.

fields.name: onGround
fields.desc: True if the player is on the ground

notes: S03PacketPlayer is the abstract base. C04/C05/C06 each have their own packet ID. The client sends C04 when only position changes, C05 when only rotation changes, and C06 when both change. onGround is ALWAYS present.

writeup.p: C03PacketPlayer is the abstract base of the serverbound movement family: four registered packet ids (0x03 bare, 0x04 position, 0x05 look, 0x06 pos+look) share one class with subclasses, and the vanilla client emits one of them every tick from EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer. The payload is a single onGround byte plus optional x/y/z doubles and yaw/pitch floats. Every server-side movement decision derives from it: position integration, ground state, fall distance, rotation, and the server's own movement validation. It is the most-sent packet in the play state and by far the most-abused one in the 8-client corpus, which references it in over 300 mined locations.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer snapshots lastPos, computes the squared delta, and arms a hasMoved flag on the first small movement. Position values beyond +-3.0E7 on X or Z kick with "Illegal position". A reported Y of -999.0 disables the movement flag entirely (the client sends it when falling out of the world). The vanilla anti-cheat is the "moved too quickly" check: the sum of min(|delta|, |motion|) squared per axis must stay under 100.0, otherwise the player is teleported back with a warning. A residual delta over 0.0625 squared after moveEntity logs "moved wrongly" and snaps the player back. If the client reports onGround=false while the server thinks the player is grounded and Y is rising, the server calls jump(). Fall damage is applied from the server's own simulated fall state, which is what ground spoofing attacks.

The corpus splits into five families. Ground-state spoofers: NoFall in all eight clients, plus FastUse and Regen that send C03(true) or bare C03() to force the server-side regen tick. Movement engines: Flight (Nekoware, Rise 5.99, the 13+ mode Rise 6.x flight suite, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity), Speed and Bhop (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma, Spicy), Step (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma), Phase (Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x NormalPhase, Sigma). Buffer and replay: Blink in Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x components, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity. Position injection: Criticals offset ladders, TPAura and Infinite path walks, Damage utilities, AntiVoid, LongJump, and teleport modules. Disablers: Memeware, Rise 5.99, the Rise 6.x per-server suite, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity all rewrite, cancel or re-inject C03 to break anti-cheat position timing.

onGround is a single trusted bit that drives server-side jump physics and fall-damage accumulation: NoFall reports ground every tick so the server's entity never accrues fall distance. The 100.0 and 0.0625 squared-delta gates are the real vanilla anti-cheat, so every movement module must keep reported deltas under them or accept the teleport-back. The -999.0 Y sentinel is a free pass for vertical state: modules and commands use it to reset position without moving the player. Disablers weaponize the packet stream itself: cancelling C03 while Hypixel's watchdog is armed freezes the player server-side, and rewriting C06 into C04 (or the reverse) breaks anti-cheats that count packet-type ratios. Rotation is never validated against motion in vanilla, so spinbot and rotation-spoof modules can report any yaw/pitch.

implementation.overview: The movement spine of 1.8.9: one onGround byte plus optional position and rotation, emitted 20 times a second, trusted by the server for position integration, jump physics and fall damage. NoFall ground-spoofs it, Flight/Speed/Step/Phase forge its coordinates, Blink buffers it, Criticals and Damage inject offset ladders into it, and the disabler suites cancel or rewrite it to freeze the server-side player.
implementation.server_handling: processPlayer runs on the server thread and, for position-carrying variants, compares the packet position against the stored lastPos. The hasMoved gate requires the first reported movement to be under 0.25 squared before any validation starts. The "moved too quickly" check uses min(|delta|, |motion|) per axis, so large instantaneous deltas are masked by small motion values; the check teleports back via setPlayerLocation instead of kicking. "moved wrongly" fires when the post-integration residual exceeds 0.0625 squared and the player is not sleeping or in creative, also teleporting back. When the client reports onGround=false while the server-side player is grounded and Y is rising, the server calls jump(), which is the mechanism both criticals and the watchdog-disabler +0.16/+0.07 packet pairs exploit. The flight check runs when the player has no block collision under the bounding box and flight is disabled, kicking on sustained airborne motion.
implementation.protocol_notes: Four distinct ids map to one class: C03PacketPlayer (onGround only), C04PacketPlayerPosition (+x,y,z), C05PacketPlayerLook (+yaw,pitch), C06PacketPlayerPosLook (+both). The moving flag (field_149480_h) is set by the position constructors and the rotating flag by the look constructors; writePacketData emits the onGround byte first, then the doubles and floats conditionally. The -999.0 Y convention is a wire-level sentinel: the client sends C06 with y=-999 when falling out of the world, and the server clears the moving flag when it sees it. EntityPlayerSP selects the subclass by what changed this tick, and NetHandlerPlayClient answers S08 teleports with a C06 confirming the new position.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP checks ground-state consistency (onGround true while falling), horizontal acceleration for speed, vertical acceleration for flight, and packet gaps for blink. Verus and AAC correlate rotation with motion, which is why Rise 6.x's PacketNoRotate rewrites C06 into C04 to strip rotations. Hypixel's watchdog is fought with the ground-truth +0.16/+0.07 jump-flag pair followed by full C03 cancellation for the watchdog window, disarmed by S08. Grim and Vulcan target packet-order and buffer abuse, countered by Rise 6.x modes like BufferAbuseFlight and the ConvertMovingPackets disabler. Timer-based flight and bhop (Spicy's 26.5 tps) flag timer checks unless the keepalive and transaction streams are delayed in lockstep, which is the disabler's second job.

modules.name: NoFall
modules.purpose: Eliminate fall damage by reporting onGround=true while falling, so the server-side entity never accumulates fall distance.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware's Hypixel mode fires C03(true) through sendPacketSilent (bus-bypassing) the moment fallDistance reaches 2 with ground below, then resets the local fallDistance; the Ground Spoof mode mutates the UpdateEvent ground flag so the vanilla emitter sends onGround=true in every packet while falling past 2.5 blocks. The two modes cover servers that do and do not validate extra packets.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent; the injected C03(true) bypasses the packet event bus.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: NCP's ground check compares onGround against the simulated fall state; reporting ground mid-air is its classic flag, so packet-based NoFall is mostly caught by modern checks while ground-spoof variants that keep the arc believable last longer.
modules.variations: Nekoware sends C03(true) via sendPacketSilent on the same condition. Rise 5.99 sends C03(true) or a C06 with onGround true. Rise 6.x splits PacketNoFall (C03 true), FlagNoFall (C06 response spoof), PlaceNoFall, VulcanAndVerusNoFall and WatchdogNoFall. Sigma and Spicy send C03(true) on fallDistance thresholds; Tenacity's NoFallModule appears in the corpus via import only.

modules.name: Flight / Fly
modules.purpose: Move vertically and horizontally without the server's flight permission, by driving client physics and shaping the C03 stream the vanilla emitter sends.
modules.how_it_works: Nekoware's Vanilla mode sets motionY from input and horizontal speed directly and sends nothing, using a fall/ascend C04 pair every 700ms as anti-kick. Damage mode floods C0CPacketInput plus C03(true) each pre tick and starts with the fall-damage C04 ladder (y+3.05, y, y+0.41999998688697815) to gain the damage boost that defeats NCP flight checks. Verus mode places a C08 block below and zeroes motionY. The PacketOutEvent handler cancels C0F and C00 so the position stream is not correlated against transaction timing.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent for physics, PacketOutEvent for the keepalive/transaction cancel, onEnable for the damage ladder.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The damage ladder leaves a fallDistance anomaly and requires taking fall damage at enable; the periodic anti-kick packets produce a Y sawtooth that NCP's flight check averages out over time. Cancelling C0F/C00 freezes ping and transaction state, which itself is a flag on transaction-aware servers.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Fly is a 2000+ line multi-mode module covering packet, ground, damage, S08-cancel and anti-cheat-specific variants. Rise 6.x ships 13+ named flight modes (AstralMC, BlockDrop, BufferAbuse, Creative, Funcraft, Grim, LatestNCP, MMC, MineLand, Vulcan, Watchdog). Sigma's Fly has multiple packet modes plus PremiumFlyAddon. Spicy's Fly mirrors BackupFly's 0.0624986421/0.0625/0.0000013579 C04 offset ladder. Tenacity's FlightModule sends C04 +0.3/+0.1 offsets and C03(false).

modules.name: Blink
modules.purpose: Freeze the server-side player by buffering every C03 (or every packet) and replaying the queue in order on disable, creating fake lag.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, with All Packets on, every outgoing packet is parked in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue and cancelled; with it off only C03PacketPlayer (and its subclasses) is held. Pulse mode flushes the queue every N ticks with a 10% random skip to bound the blink windows. onDisable replays everything with sendPacketWithoutEvent in FIFO order. An optional EntityOtherPlayerMP renders the frozen position to other players.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Any anti-cheat that measures the gap between movement packets flags long blinks; pulse mode bounds the gap and the random skip breaks periodicity. The flushed burst is also a tell, since the server sees a jump in position on release.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x moves this into BlinkComponent and MovementBlinkComponent (position-only) shared by Blink, BlinkAntiVoid and WatchdogAntiVoid. Sigma's Blink cancels C03 and C00 together on outgoing pre. Spicy's Blink cancels outgoing packets on its EventSendPacket. Tenacity's Blink event handles the C04/C05/C06 subclasses separately.

modules.name: Step
modules.purpose: Climb blocks higher than the vanilla 0.6 limit by reporting intermediate C04 positions that hide the vertical delta.
modules.how_it_works: Nekoware's NCP mode watches the ClimbSlabEvent; when the bounding box has risen past 0.6, it sends C04 at y+0.42 and y+0.75 with onGround false, then drops timerSpeed to 0.4 for two ticks so the faster climb does not trip horizontal speed checks. Vanilla mode just sets stepHeight locally. The 0.42/0.75 pair mirrors the NCP speed/bhop arc, which is why the module refuses to run while the client's Speed module is on.
modules.vanilla_hook: ClimbSlabEvent for the packet ladder; UpdateEvent for stepHeight and timer restore.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server accepts the ladder because each reported position is within one tick's plausible delta; the timer slowdown hides the effective vertical speed. Checks that simulate stepping independently (Matrix, Vulcan) flag the 1.0-block rise regardless of the ladder.
modules.variations: Memeware's Step is the same packet ladder lineage. Rise 5.99 sends C04 at d plus random/2000. Rise 6.x splits NCPStep (d plus random/2000), NewNCPStep, MatrixStep (exact float ladder 0.41999998688698, 0.7531999805212, 1.00133597911215, 1.42133596599913, 1.75453595963335, 2.0026719582243), VulcanStep (single +0.5) and WatchdogStep (packet rewrite). Sigma sends first/second/off C04 ladders plus a C06 look variant.

modules.name: Speed / Bhop
modules.purpose: Move faster than vanilla sprint by manipulating jump arcs, timer speed and the movement packets the client emits.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy's Bhop Hypixel mode sets noClip, jumps on a 0.00004 ground check, and runs 26.5 tps plus random jitter in air so the vanilla C03 emission carries an accelerated trajectory. Test 3 mode drives EventMove directly: motionY 0.41999998688697815 on ground, speed seeded at forward*2.1500000953674316 and decayed by speed/165 per air tick, plus a random 1.0E-5..9.9E-4 Y jitter on ground packets. An S08 setback counter auto-disables after 3 lagbacks in 5 seconds.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventMove and EventMotion for physics; EventPacket on S08 for the lagback counter.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The 0.42 jump plus speed decay is the classic NCP bhop signature; the timer manipulation (26.5 tps) trips timer checks unless keepalive and transaction packets are delayed to match. The S08 auto-disable is an explicit flag-avoidance mechanism: the module quits before the anti-cheat can accumulate a ban.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Speed has NCP/LowHop-style modes that send C04 ground packets at specific moments. Rise 6.x ships FuncraftSpeed and InteractSpeed, which send C04 with onGround true on interact. Sigma's Bhop sends C04(x, -10, z, true) as a void trick, with PremiumBhopAddon extending it.

modules.name: Disabler
modules.purpose: Break anti-cheat position timing by cancelling, rewriting or re-injecting C03 packets, usually paired with keepalive and transaction manipulation.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma's Hypixel mode arms a watchdog flag by sending C04 (x, y+0.16, z, true) and (x, y+0.07, z, true) through sendPacketNoEvent, then cancels every C03 in the outgoing pre phase until an S08PacketPlayerPosLook disarms it. ViperMC mode injects ten C04 packets alternating +-0.2 Y every 3 seconds. The keepalive and transaction branches (Erisium re-sends the last S00 key every 1500ms, SagePvP/ColdNetwork cancel accepted C0F with id 0) keep the frozen connection alive.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket outgoing pre for C03 cancel and C04 injection; EventUpdate for the arming sequence.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The +0.16/+0.07 pair is the Hypixel watchdog jump-flag trigger, a ground-truth pattern the server accepts as a jump; the resulting 5 second free-move window is bounded by the watchdog itself. Cancelling C03 while armed freezes the server-side player, which is the point, and the S08 disarm prevents the freeze from persisting.
modules.variations: Memeware's Disabler has Mineplex Combat (C00 key corruption), Transaction, Latest Verus, PvPTemple, OmegaCraft, Timer, AACv1.9.10, Sloth, Ghostly, Watchdog and Faithful Movement modes. Rise 5.99's Disabler rewrites C06 into C04 and re-injects position packets. Rise 6.x ships ConvertMovingPackets, DynamicPVP, Ghostly, Lunar, NoRules, RiseBalance, Teleport, UniversoCraft and Verus2 disablers, most of which convert C03 subclasses or re-send position. Spicy has Disabler and Hypixel5SecDisabler (C04 +0.21/+0.11 pattern). Tenacity has DisablerModule and AdvancedDisablerModule with C06 to C04 conversion.

implementation.general_hooks: Every client intercepts C03 at the outgoing packet event (PacketOutEvent, PacketSendEvent, EventSendPacket) and matches instanceof C03PacketPlayer, which also catches the C04/C05/C06 subclasses. Movement engines hook UpdateEvent or PreMotionEvent to alter position, ground and rotation before the vanilla emitter builds the packet; Rise 6.x additionally routes through TeleportEvent for S08 responses.
implementation.client_variations: Vanilla emission differs per client: Memeware and Nekoware patch EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer to fire a custom UpdateEvent that carries setY/setGround, Sigma and Spicy do the same with their motion events, while Rise 5.99 and Tenacity rewrite the emitter to consume their own event objects. Send paths diverge the same way: sendQueue.addToSendQueue (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity), PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketWithoutEvent (Rise 5.99), PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent (Rise 6.x). Bus-bypassing sends (sendPacketSilent, sendPacketNoEvent, sendPacketWithoutEvent, sendNoEvent) are universal and used whenever a module must not re-trigger its own packet listener.
